detail.body: - [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. # What does this PR do? Associated with: https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/3920 - Extend image modality to support video modalities in Megatron-Inference. - Modalities - Images can be either shipped into the completions endpoint as raw bytes (`{"image": [image1_bytes, image2_bytes]}`), or passed `Megatron(Async)LLM.generate` as preprocessed Tensors (`{"image": {"imgs": ..., "imgs_sizes": ..., "num_tiles": ..., "num_img_embeddings_per_tile": ...}}`). - Video can be either shipped into the completions endpoint as raw bytes (`{"video": [video1_bytes, video2_bytes]}`) or a byte-string containing paths to video frame images (`VideoProcessingConfig.frame_manifest_magic + json.dumps({"frame_paths": [...]}).encode("utf-8")`), or passed to `Megatron(Async)LLM.generate` as preprocessed Tensors (`{"video": {"imgs": ..., "imgs_sizes": ..., "num_frames": ... }}`). - Pre-processed Tensors can be optionally pre-expanded with multimodal placeholders by RL or the user using the config `media_tokens_preexpanded: bool` in the `multi_modal_data` dictionary input to `Megatron(Async)LLM.generate`. - In a nutshell, pre-processed + pre-expanded Tensors = NeMo-RL non-Gym handles the multimodal preprocessing, while bytes = NeMo-RL Gym sends over the raw data for Megatron-Inference to handle the multimodal preprocessing. Having direct engine access in the first (Tensor) case is generally something we want to keep maintaining, not only to support non-Gym in RL but also for users to have direct control over what Tensors go into the encoder/decoder. - If you ever see the term "compact" describing prompt tokens it means "prior to expansion" where we have a single token placeholder representing an image or frame or video that will be expanded into many placeholder multimodal tokens for embedding injection before generation. This form is stored and used in some situations where we want to return a non-negative prompt of tokens back to RL and also in multi-turn chat where we re-tokenize and re-expand these compact prompts for chat continuation. - These match existing NeMo-RL vLLM API's for multimodal. (But it's honestly a mess of possible inputs depending on what each multimodal dataset prefers...) - Just like images, the video embeddings are computed in `_build_vlm_request` before the controller takes over decoding, and the embedding installed in the request can be used for checkpointing, etc. I hope I didn't unintentionally change too much for the trunk of the decoder engine here. - Caching / Routing - A cache key is computed here depending on the bytes: `inference_request.py/compute_media_cache_key` - Support media affinity via cache key in coordinator routing, which mixes into the affinity score produced by prefix hits for text. - Support vision embedding caching to skip the encoder pass on subsequent generations. The cache is LRU-cleared and cleared on suspend. - Salt in a media cache key in `compute_block_hashes_batched` to make prefix caching aware of the multimodal data in the prompt as well. - Note to self: `DynamicVLMInferenceRequest` saves the media key into the context and this is used later (`_compute_block_hashes`) to salt and recompute the engine-internal KV cache hash, which uses the expanded prompt with `` - Inference wrappers have a few more methods that are common to multimodal: `supports_` for quick-checking what a wrapper can support for a model, `MultimodalPromptConfig` and `resolve_media_token_id` for looking up what image/video placeholders and token IDs should be for a model so that the inference engine can use them as embedding placeholders in `expand_image_tokens` called by `_build_vlm_request`. This is a very _**experimental**_ API for inference wrappers. - Added a new inference wrapper for Nemotron Omni: `NemotronOmniInferenceWrapper`. - Also updated `VLMInferenceWrapper` for video and LLaVA. - `dynamic_res_preprocess` has been updated to support multiple ways of patching frames, and `video_maintain_aspect_ratio=True` is required for parity with RL + vLLM. - For video frames, we only sample up to `num_frames` so we can sample first, then convert the sampled frames to PIL / Tensor. For both images and video, we have vLLM parity: https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=nwusercye_nv Log prob error, gradient norms, and gen KL error all look reasonable as well, with some noise. In the RL NSight profile, multimodal embeddings are computed once per prompt group and cached for future use, and then subsequent forward passes are decoder-only, all overlapped with RL training for async non-colocated (trajectory age = 2): There's a known issue with this gap appearing in the generation loop, will debug in a future PR. # Bugs - Added back LLaVA audio support which seems to have been reverted for not much reason, referring to this PR: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/4402 -> https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6260 # Testing - RL - https://github.com/cspades/RL/blob/cye/rl_mllm_omni_multimodal_scripts/scripts has 1N and 8N scripts with easy swapping between vLLM and MLLM. - E2E Multimodal Inference - Run `examples/inference/*_multimodal_infer.py` on 2 GPUs with at least 40 GB. (For me, my two A6000's.) ``` uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 8 -m pytest -vvs tests/unit_tests/inference ========= 2601 passed, 108 skipped, 2872 warnings in 971.37s (0:16:11) ========== ``` :warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall. ## Contribution process ### Pre-checks - [x] I have added relevant unit tests - [ ] I have added relevant functional tests - [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html) - [ ] I have added relevant documentation - [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR ### Code review Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged! All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft. #### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review" 1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**. 2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes. - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`. :warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing. Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled. #### Step 2: Final Review For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned. For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped. #### Step 3: Approved Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**. ### Merge Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

+    imgs_sizes: torch.Tensor,
+    patch_dim: int,
+    *,
+    pixel_shuffle: bool,
+    pixel_shuffle_size: int = 2,
+    spatial_merge_size: int = 1,
+) -> list[int]:
+    """Return projected token counts for dynamic-resolution media frames."""
+    if patch_dim <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("patch_dim must be greater than 0.")
+    if imgs_sizes.ndim != 2 or imgs_sizes.shape[1] != 2:
+        raise ValueError(f"imgs_sizes must have shape [N, 2], got {tuple(imgs_sizes.shape)}.")
+    if pixel_shuffle and pixel_shuffle_size <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("pixel_shuffle_size must be greater than 0.")
+    if spatial_merge_size <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("spatial_merge_size must be greater than 0.")
+
+    counts = []
+    for height, width in imgs_sizes.tolist():
+        if height % patch_dim or width % patch_dim:
+            raise ValueError("Media dimensions must be divisible by patch_dim.")
+        patch_height = height // patch_dim
+        patch_width = width // patch_dim
+        if pixel_shuffle and (
+            patch_height % pixel_shuffle_size or patch_width % pixel_shuffle_size
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Media patch grids must be divisible by pixel_shuffle_size.")

+        if pixel_shuffle:
+            count //= pixel_shuffle_size**2
+        merge_factor = spatial_merge_size**2
+        if count % merge_factor:
+            raise ValueError("Media token count must be divisible by the spatial merge factor.")

+    return counts

**[CRITICAL Correctness]** `_collapse_expanded_media_tokens` is a no-op on the token ids this path actually receives, so multi-turn multimodal chat with `prevent_retokenization` produces a corrupt prefix.

**What:** `last_assistant_message["prompt_token_ids"]` is `result["prompt_tokens"]`, i.e. the *engine's* expanded prompt. In `_build_vlm_request` the expansion pads with `-1` and only rewrites those pads to a real vocabulary id when `_resolve_image_token_id()` returns non-`None` — and that helper deliberately returns `None` for negative sentinels (`dynamic_engine.py:1514-1528`, LLaVA's `image_token_index = -200`). Meanwhile `_media_model_token_ids` returns `{-200}`. So the collapse looks for `-200` in a sequence that contains runs of `-1` and collapses nothing.

**Why it matters:** `previous_turn_token_ids` keeps hundreds of `-1` pads where `retokenized_previous_turn_token_ids` has a single marker, and `_replace_prefix_tokens` returns that pad-laden prefix as the new prompt. The next turn's prompt therefore contains zero `-200` markers, so `expand_image_tokens` finds no media position and the request either fails the new `Expanded prompt has 0 media-token position(s), but the vision encoder produced N embedding(s)` check or silently answers about an image the model never attended to. This is the primary multi-turn VLM/video path.

**Fix:** collapse on the pad value actually present, not just the configured marker. Resolve the engine's effective media filler the same way the engine does (real id when non-negative, `-1` otherwise) and pass both to `_collapse_expanded_media_tokens`; alternatively return the compact form to the client for stitching instead of reconstructing it. Please add a multi-turn test that round-trips `prompt_token_ids` from an actual `_build_vlm_request` expansion rather than a hand-written `-200` sequence.

**[CRITICAL Correctness]** The collapse also merges *adjacent distinct* placeholders, not just runs of one expanded marker.

**What:** the guard is `token_id in media_token_ids and token_id == previous_token_id`. Since image and video specs frequently share the same `model_token_id` (`VLMInferenceWrapper.get_multimodal_prompt_config` returns the *same* `MediaPromptSpec` for both), two legitimately separate media placeholders that happen to be adjacent — e.g. two tubelet markers, or two images with no text between them — collapse into one. **What:** `image_token_index` defaults to `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TOKEN_INDEX = -200` (`llava_model.py:49,127`). **[IMPORTANT Correctness]** The vision-embedding cache validates a hit only by embedding *count*, which is far too weak for a cache keyed on media bytes alone.

**What:** `media_cache_key` is a sha256 over the raw media bytes only (`inference_request.py:122-134`; the digest mixes in `b"megatron-media-v1\0"`, the modality, and per-item lengths — nothing else). But the projected embeddings depend on more than the bytes: the resolved target resolution, `num_frames` / sampling, `temporal_patch_size`, `media_tokens_preexpanded`, and the model weights. The only guard on reuse is `cached_embedding_count != expected_embedding_count`.

**Why it matters:** the same video submitted twice with different `num_frames` (or against a differently-configured `VideoProcessingConfig`, or where a prompt supplies per-tubelet vs. per-video placeholders) can produce the *same* embedding count while the embeddings themselves are wrong for the second request. The engine then serves a completion conditioned on the wrong visual content and reports success — the same class of silent cross-request contamination the surrounding comment at lines 1676-1683 says prefix caching was disabled to prevent.

**Fix:** mix the preprocessing-affecting parameters into the key rather than validating after the fact. Extend `key_for_bytes` to hash `num_frames`, the effective `VideoProcessingConfig` (num_frames, temporal_patch_size, and the `ImageProcessingConfig` fields that determine resolution), and `media_tokens_preexpanded`. Keep the count check as a cheap backstop, but it should be an `assert`/raise on mismatch rather than a silent recompute, since a mismatch now means the key was wrong.

**What:** `media_cache_key` is set for every raw-bytes multimodal request regardless of whether the vision cache is enabled, so `isinstance(media_cache_key, str)` is true on essentially all of them and `get_media_affine_data_parallel_rank` fully replaces the scored router.

**[IMPORTANT Performance]** Every frame of the video is decoded and materialized as a PIL image before sampling throws almost all of them away.

**What:** the list comprehension over `container.decode(video=0)` decodes the entire stream, then `sample_indices` keeps at most `config.num_frames` (default 8) of them.

**Why it matters:** a 60 s clip at 30 fps is 1800 frames; at 720p that is ~3.7 GB of resident `PIL.Image` RGB data to select 8 frames, on the server's request path. It's an easy OOM with a couple of concurrent video requests and it scales with clip length rather than with `num_frames`. `frame.to_image()` per frame also costs a full RGB conversion for frames that are immediately discarded.

**Fix:** decode lazily. Use the container's frame count / duration (`stream.frames`, or `duration * average_rate`) to compute the target indices up front, then either seek (`container.seek`) to each target or iterate and call `to_image()` only on indices in the target set:

```python
with av.open(io.BytesIO(encoded_video)) as container:
    stream = container.streams.video[0]
    total = stream.frames or 0
    if total > 0:
        wanted = set(compute_sample_indices(total, sample_count))
        frames = [
            frame.to_image().convert("RGB")
            for index, frame in enumerate(container.decode(stream))
            if index in wanted
        ]
```

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** The subscription barrier counts frames, not distinct peers, so a reconnect can release it early.

**What:** the loop increments `subscribed_peers` for every `b"\x01"` frame received. ZMQ SUB sockets re-send their subscriptions on reconnect, and `XPUB_VERBOSE` is set precisely so duplicates are *not* coalesced. If one peer's TCP connection flaps during startup — plausible at scale, which is when this deadlock shows up — its second subscription counts as a new peer and the leader proceeds while another rank has not yet subscribed. That is the same deadlock this commit is fixing, now with a rarer trigger.

**Why it matters:** silent, load-dependent, and the failure mode is a hang rather than an error, which is expensive to debug in a large job.

**Fix:** `XPUB` subscription frames don't carry peer identity, so counting can't be made exact on this socket alone. Two options: (a) set `ZMQ_XPUB_NODROP`/track via a `ROUTER` side-channel where each peer sends one identified "subscribed" message, or (b) keep the count as a fast path and follow it with a `dist.barrier(group=process_group)` plus one throwaway publish that peers acknowledge, so correctness rests on the collective rather than on frame arithmetic.

Separately, on scope: this commit is the head of a PR titled "Support video modality in Megatron-Inference" and is unrelated to video. Per `docs/developer/contribute.md` ("Split your changes into separate, atomic commits… Touch anything outside the stated scope of the PR" is in the Don't list), this ZMQ fix should be its own PR — it's a startup-deadlock fix that reviewers of a video feature won't scrutinize, and it can land much faster on its own. See `.claude/skills/mcore-split-pr/SKILL.md`.

**[SUGGESTION Simplification]** `slot[0] in str(messages_to_last_assistant_message)` selects previous-turn slots by substring-matching a `repr()` of the message list.

**What:** `str()` on a list of dicts produces a Python `repr`, and the sentinel is then searched for anywhere in it. It works because `__MCORE_MEDIA_SLOT_{i}__` is unlikely to collide, but it depends on `repr` formatting, scans the entire rendered conversation per slot (O(slots × conversation size)), and would also match a sentinel appearing in an unexpected field.

**Why it matters:** this is the input to `_tokenize_with_media_slots`, which asserts each sentinel appears exactly once in the rendered template — so a mis-selected slot list turns into a `ValueError` on a legitimate request.

**Fix:** the slots were created in message order, so the split point is structural rather than textual. Have `_extract_multimodal_from_messages` record the originating message index alongside each slot (`(sentinel, modality, message_index)`), then select with `slot[2] <= last_assistant_message_idx`. That's exact, O(slots), and independent of `repr`.

**[SUGGESTION Simplification]** `65536` is a hardcoded, undocumented capacity for an unbounded-lifetime map.

**What:** every distinct media key ever routed adds an entry; eviction is LRU at 64Ki. There's no comment explaining the choice and no way to tune it, while the sibling knobs (`max_requests`, `prefix_caching_routing_alpha`, `vision_embedding_cache_max_bytes`) are all config-driven.

**Why it matters:** 64Ki `str → bytes` entries is single-digit MB, so this is a maintainability point rather than a leak. But the value is only meaningful relative to the engines' `vision_embedding_cache_max_bytes` — retaining affinity for keys the engines have long since evicted just pins load without any cache benefit.

**Fix:** name the constant at module scope with a one-line rationale tying it to the engine-side cache, and/or accept it as a coordinator argument. Also worth pruning entries for a rank in `_remove_engine` (lines 291-320 already rebuild `_hash_table` there) — the membership guard in `get_media_affine_data_parallel_rank` tolerates stale identities, but leaving them means an evicted rank's keys each cost one wasted lookup and re-assignment.

**[IMPORTANT Correctness]** The new tests mock out the two methods that implement the feature they'd otherwise cover, so the vision-embedding cache has no test at all.

**What:** `_get_cached_vision_embedding` is stubbed to always return `None` and `_cache_vision_embedding` is a bare `Mock`. Every one of the three new tests therefore exercises only the cache-miss path. Nothing covers the byte-budget accounting, LRU eviction, the `cached_embedding_count != expected_embedding_count` invalidation branch, or — most importantly — the three lifecycle clears (`reset()`, `suspend()`, and the generation-epoch change in `schedule_requests()`).

**Why it matters:** the `suspend()` clear carries the comment "A suspend may be followed by an in-place weight refit. Projected media embeddings are weight-dependent and must never cross it." Serving stale embeddings across a refit is a silent wrong-answer bug in an RL loop, and it's exactly the kind of thing that regresses when someone later reorders `suspend()`. It is also cheap to test — the cache is a plain `OrderedDict` of tensors keyed by string.

**Fix:** add direct tests for the cache helpers (no engine mock needed beyond `vision_embedding_cache_max_bytes`): insert past the byte budget and assert LRU eviction; insert an oversized tensor and assert it is not cached; then assert `_vision_embedding_cache` is empty after `reset()`, after `suspend()`, and after a generation-epoch bump. Given `_get_cached_vision_embedding` returns `None` when the budget is 0, one test should also cover the enabled path end-to-end through `_build_vlm_request` with the real methods rather than mocks.

The PR's "unit tests added/updated" pre-check box is unchecked; per `.claude/skills/mcore-testing/SKILL.md` these run under `torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node 8`. There are also no functional tests or golden values for the video path — worth adding at least one `tests/functional_tests/test_cases/` case given this adds a new modality end-to-end.

issue_comments.body:
**Strict review summary — PR #6809**

**Findings: CRITICAL: 5 · IMPORTANT: 16 · SUGGESTION: 5** (26 inline comments)

Reviewed all 26 changed files against `origin/main` at head `08b5d38`. This is a substantial, generally careful feature — the inline comments explaining *why* a decision was made (prefix-cache disabling for image requests, the `suspend()` cache clear, the tubelet grouping) are genuinely useful and above the norm for this area. The findings below are concentrated in three places: the multi-turn chat path, the temporal branch in `LLaVAModel.forward`, and video preprocessing.

**Most impactful**

**1. Multi-turn multimodal chat is broken (two independent CRITICAL bugs, same code path).**
`_collapse_expanded_media_tokens` is a no-op on the tokens it actually receives: `prompt_token_ids` comes back from the engine containing `-1` pads (the engine deliberately refuses to substitute LLaVA's negative `image_token_index` — `dynamic_engine.py:1514-1528`), while the collapse looks for `-200`. The stitched prefix therefore keeps hundreds of pads, and the next turn has zero media markers. Independently, the collapse condition merges *adjacent distinct* placeholders, which the PR's own `[[11, -200, -200, 12]]` test case demonstrates. Both fail silently or as a spurious embedding-count `ValueError`.

**2. `get_multimodal_prompt_config` publishes `-200` as a real token id.**
`_tokenize_with_media_slots` appends it verbatim into tokens that get hashed, detokenized, and returned to clients; and when the tokenizer *does* define `<image>`, the `token_id != resolved_id` check 400s every multimodal chat request on a correctly-configured LLaVA deployment. The fix is a two-line change: only surface non-negative ids, let `None` mean "resolve from tokenizer".

**3. `num_frames` is silently ignored when `temporal_patch_dim == 1`, where `main` raised `NotImplementedError`.**
Reachable from the new server: `temporal_patch_size` defaults to 1 for non-temporal models, and `add_request` enters the VLM path on `num_frames` alone. Pointing the video endpoint at an image VLM now silently produces per-frame image embeddings instead of an error. Related: `num_frames` without `imgs` degrades to a text-only generation.

**4. `fp8_enabled=False` hardcoded in the temporal CP split while `fp8_recipe` is passed through.**
The two arguments contradict each other; `fp8_recipe` only selects the padding multiple that `fp8_enabled` gates. FP8 vision + CP>1 + video gets unpadded local shards. The constructor already computes the right value at line 353. No test covers CP>1 on this path.

**5. `pixel_shuffle` numerics change for non-square grids affects existing image inference.**
`main`'s non-square branch was a pure reshape; it is now full 2x2 spatial grouping plus a new divisibility assert, and `pixel_shuffle_dynamic_res` delegates to it. The rewritten test confirms both halves. I read this as an intentional fix, so the ask is disclosure + golden values, not reversion — but it needs to be called out as breaking, and the divergence from `examples/mimo/model_providers/radio_encoder.py:131` ("e2e-validated; do not swap to match it") reconciled.

**Also worth attention**

- **Cache safety:** `media_cache_key` hashes media bytes only, but embeddings depend on `num_frames`, resolution, and `temporal_patch_size`. The sole reuse guard is embedding *count*, which collides easily. Mix the preprocessing parameters into the key.
- **Video preprocessing:** the full stream is decoded to PIL before sampling frames (GBs for a 1-minute 720p clip); `reference_hw` from the first video is applied to all videos in the batch (silent aspect distortion); `_video_target_resolution` ignores `spatial_merge_size` and `min_patches` and lacks the `<= max_patches` assert that `dynamic_res_preprocess` has.
- **Untrusted input:** data-URL video bypasses `_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` entirely (that cap only guards the http branch) — and video is *required* to be a data URL. `_load_frame_sequence_manifest` reads arbitrary local paths from request payloads with no root confinement; opt-in and off by default, but it needs a configured root before anyone enables it.
- **Sync / CUDA-graph:** `.item()` inside `LLaVAModel.forward` (line 1331) plus two in `_build_vlm_request`, all avoidable — the counts are known host-side. `_build_vlm_request` visibly tries to stay sync-free (see its own comment at 1572-1575).
- **Routing:** since `media_cache_key` is always set, *every* multimodal request now bypasses the scored `get_best_data_parallel_rank` for an affinity router whose only load signal is `pending < max_requests`. `_remove_engine` also rebuilds `_hash_table` but not `_media_cache_affinity`.
- **Mandatory unused-identifier check** found three write-only additions: `supports_text/image/video/audio` (declared + assigned, zero readers — they look like the capability gate that would have prevented finding 3), `MultimodalPromptConfig.from_dict` (no callers), `DynamicInferenceRequest.compact_prompt_tokens` (written and merged, never read).

**Process**

- **All five pre-check boxes are unchecked** (unit tests, functional tests, typing, docs, autoformat), and there is **no linked issue** for a new modality. Import order in the two new test files is not isort-clean — run `uv run isort` per CLAUDE.md, then `BASE_REF=main CHECK_ONLY=true bash tools/autoformat.sh`.
- **Test coverage gap:** the new engine tests mock out `_get_cached_vision_embedding` / `_cache_vision_embedding`, so the vision cache — including the `suspend()`-clear that prevents serving stale embeddings across a weight refit — is entirely untested. No functional tests or golden values for the video path.
- **Scope:** the head commit (ZMQ XPUB subscription handshake) is unrelated to video and would land faster as its own PR. It also has a correctness issue of its own: it counts `b"\x01"` frames rather than distinct peers, so a startup reconnect can release the barrier early.

**Risk assessment: High**

Not because the design is wrong — the temporal/tubelet approach and the packed dynamic-res plumbing look sound — but because four of the five CRITICAL findings are silent-wrong-answer paths reachable from the default server configuration, and the new code touches `LLaVAModel.forward` and `pixel_shuffle`, which existing image-only VLM deployments depend on. Findings 1-3 and 5 should block; 4 needs either the config-derived value or an explicit `NotImplementedError`. I would want the vision-cache tests and at least one video functional test with golden values before merge, plus the two compat changes (`pixel_shuffle` numerics, `num_image_tiles` default) documented in the PR description.
